tools.name: privi_token_market
tools.description:
PRIVI on Base: price, how much PRIVI and USDC the Privi swap desk holds (so whether a swap can fill),
any Uniswap v3 / Aerodrome pools, and optionally a swap quote. Every paid Privi tool also accepts PRIVI. Free.

tools.name: ledger_pricing
tools.description: List Privi Ledger tools, what each costs, and how to get an organization key.

tools.name: ledger_check_receipt
tools.description: Confirm that an action receipt exists in the ledger and when it was recorded. Reveals no action contents. Free.

tools.name: ledger_audit_stream
tools.description:
Check whether an agent's action log is intact: entry count, time span, action and failure
counts, head hash, and where tampering broke the chain if it did. Does not reveal the actions
themselves. Paid per call via x402.

tools.name: ledger_record_action
tools.description:
Append an action to the organization's tamper-evident log. Returns the entry with its
entry_hash receipt. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_read_stream
tools.description:
Read your organization's entries in a stream, oldest first, with an integrity check of the
whole stream. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_list_streams
tools.description: List your organization's streams with entry counts. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_compliance_report
tools.description:
Audit-ready report of your AI agents' activity for a period (SOC 2 evidence, security
questionnaires, AI-regulation record keeping): actions by type, failures, human approvals,
log integrity, on-chain status, and findings. The report's hash is anchored on the Privi
blockchain so it cannot be edited

tools.name: ledger_report_pdf
tools.description:
A finished PDF of a sealed compliance report, for auditors and customers. Returned as base64
(pdf_base64) and as an embedded PDF resource; also downloadable at /reports/<report_id>.pdf with the
organization key. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_verify_report
tools.description:
Check that a compliance report is unaltered: recomputes its hash, confirms Privi Ledger issued it,
and checks the anchor on chain (Base, until the Privi chain mainnet). Free; no key needed.

tools.name: ledger_signup
tools.description:
Create a Privi Ledger organization on the free plan and get its API key (shown once; store it).
Free plan: up to the monthly entry limit, all tools included. Upgrade any time with
ledger_upgrade_pro. No key needed to sign up.

tools.name: ledger_plan
tools.description: Your plan, entries used this month, the limit, and when a Pro plan renews. Requires your organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_upgrade_pro
tools.description:
Buy 30 days of Privi Ledger Pro (unlimited entries) for your organization, paid in USDC on Base
via x402. Each call adds 30 days. Requires your organization API key.

tools.name: gov_ai_usecase_save
tools.description:
Add or update an entry in your agency's AI use case inventory (OMB M-25-21). Every change creates a
new version and is written to your tamper-evident 'ai-inventory' log. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gov_ai_inventory
tools.description: Your agency's AI use case inventory: the current version of each record. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gov_ai_inventory_check
tools.description:
Flags what an OMB M-25-21 review would flag before you submit: missing required fields, PII without a
Privacy Impact Assessment, and high-impact AI in pilot or deployment missing any minimum risk practice
(testing, impact assessment, independent review, monitoring, operator training, fail-safe, appe

tools.name: gov_ai_inventory_export
tools.description:
Machine-readable CSV of your publicly releasable AI use cases (for publishing at agency.gov/ai), with its
SHA-256 sealed on chain (Base, until the Privi chain mainnet) so the published file can be proven unaltered. Requires the
organization API key.

tools.name: gov_ai_verify_export
tools.description:
Check that a published AI inventory file is exactly what the agency exported from Privi Ledger, and
return its on-chain seal. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: gov_pqc_classify
tools.description:
Classify cryptographic algorithms as quantum-vulnerable (RSA, ECDH, ECDSA, EdDSA, DH, DSA, MQV),
post-quantum (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA), hybrid, symmetric/hash, or unknown. Free.

tools.name: gov_pqc_system_save
tools.description:
Record the cryptographic inventory (CBOM) of one system for post-quantum migration. Every change creates
a new version and is written to the agency's tamper-evident 'pqc-inventory' log. Scanners and agents can
submit results directly. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gov_pqc_inventory
tools.description: Current cryptographic inventory of your systems. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gov_pqc_plan
tools.description:
Prioritized post-quantum migration plan: every quantum-vulnerable asset ranked (High Value Assets,
high-impact systems and long-lived sensitive data first; key establishment before signatures), with its
deadline (key establishment Dec 31 2030, signatures Dec 31 2031), recommended NIST replacement, p

tools.name: gov_pqc_export
tools.description:
Export the full cryptographic inventory (CBOM) and migration plan as one JSON document for OMB, the
CIO or auditors, with its SHA-256 sealed on chain (Base, until the Privi chain mainnet). Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gov_pqc_verify_export
tools.description:
Check that a CBOM and migration-plan document is exactly what was exported from Privi Ledger and return
its on-chain seal. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: ledger_handshake_offer
tools.description:
Start a Privi Handshake: a two-sided record of a dealing with another company's agent
(payment, data transfer, delivery, agreement). Recorded in your log now; when the other company
accepts, both logs hold matching entries and the pair is sealed on chain (Base). Requires your
organization API key; t

tools.name: ledger_handshake_inbox
tools.description:
Handshakes sent to and from your organization, newest first, with their terms and status.
Requires your organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_handshake_accept
tools.description:
Accept a handshake addressed to your organization: records the same terms in your log, confirms
it in the other company's log, and seals the matched pair on chain (Base). Requires your
organization API key. Read the terms first with ledger_handshake_inbox.

tools.name: ledger_handshake_reject
tools.description:
Reject a handshake addressed to your organization; the other company's log records the rejection.
Requires your organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_handshake_verify
tools.description:
Public check of a handshake: both companies, status, whether both matching log entries still exist,
and the on-chain seal. Never reveals the terms. Free; useful for disputes and audits.

tools.name: passport_issue
tools.description:
Issue a Privi Passport: a signed, on-chain-anchored trust credential for your agent or organization,
scored 0-1000 (grade A-E) from verified history, integrity, anchoring, reliability, human oversight,
compliance reports and confirmed handshakes. Show it to counterparties; they verify it free with
p

tools.name: passport_verify
tools.description:
Check an AI agent's Privi Passport before trusting it: Privi signature, content unaltered, not expired or
revoked, anchor on chain (Base), and a live re-score of the agent right now (so tampering after issue
is caught). Free; no key needed.

tools.name: passport_gate
tools.description:
One-call allow/deny decision before transacting with another AI agent: verifies its Privi Passport and
applies your minimums, returning the reasons. If you send your organization API key the decision is
recorded in your own tamper-evident log as due-diligence evidence. Free.

tools.name: passport_list
tools.description: Your organization's issued passports with score, grade, expiry and revocation. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: passport_revoke
tools.description:
Revoke one of your passports (e.g. an agent was retired or compromised). Verifiers see it immediately.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: kya_check
tools.description:
Know-Your-Agent for blockchains: is this wallet operated by an audited AI agent, and how trustworthy is it
right now? Resolves the address to its organization and live Privi Passport and returns allow/deny with
reasons, plus a Privi-signed attestation (valid 60 min) you can cache. For chains, DeFi p

tools.name: kya_challenge
tools.description:
Step 1 of binding a wallet to your Privi Passport: get a message to sign with that wallet (EIP-191
personal_sign). Valid 30 minutes. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: kya_bind_wallet
tools.description:
Step 2: bind the wallet to your organization's Privi Passport so its transactions pass KYA checks. With a
wallet signature the binding is *proven*; without one it is only *declared* (most checkers require proven).
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: kya_wallets
tools.description: Wallets bound to your organization and how each was proven. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: kya_unbind_wallet
tools.description: Remove a wallet from your Passport (rotated or compromised key). KYA checks deny it immediately. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: mandate_create
tools.description:
Draft a Privi Mandate: the human's signed permission for your agent to spend, with a budget, per-payment cap,
allowed payees and expiry. Returns sign_url: send it to the human, who reads the plain-English terms and signs
once with their wallet (free, no transaction). Nothing can be spent until they

tools.name: mandate_check
tools.description:
For merchants, payment facilitators and counterparties: did a human authorize this AI agent to pay you this
amount? Verifies the human's wallet signature, status, expiry, per-payment cap, remaining budget and payee list,
and returns allow/deny with reasons plus a Privi-signed attestation. Free; no k

tools.name: mandate_spend
tools.description:
Call before each payment: checks the mandate and, if allowed, deducts the amount from the budget and records the
payment in the agent's tamper-evident log. Refused payments are logged as blocked. Refused at once if the kill switch is
on. Over the organization's live-approval threshold it returns app

tools.name: mandate_get
tools.description: Public view of a mandate: terms, status, the human's signature, spent and remaining budget, and recent spends. Free.

tools.name: mandate_list
tools.description: Your organization's mandates with status and remaining budget. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: mandate_revoke
tools.description:
Stop an agent from spending under a mandate (the human can also revoke from the sign_url page). Requires the
organization API key.

tools.name: fortress_keys
tools.description:
Privi's public signing keys: Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87 (NIST FIPS 204, CNSA 2.0 post-quantum). Pin these to
verify Privi signatures offline. Free.

tools.name: ledger_tree_head
tools.description:
The latest signed tree head of Privi's transparency log: an RFC 9162 Merkle root over every entry ever
recorded, signed with Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87, and periodically anchored on chain (Base). Free.

tools.name: ledger_inclusion_proof
tools.description:
Merkle audit path proving an entry is in Privi's append-only transparency log (RFC 9162). Verifiable offline
against the signed tree head. Reveals no entry contents. Free.

tools.name: ledger_consistency_proof
tools.description:
Proof that Privi's log only grew between two signed tree heads: nothing recorded earlier was edited, removed
or reordered (RFC 9162). Free.

tools.name: fortress_tpi_policy
tools.description:
Define a Two-Person Integrity policy: which officers can approve, and how many distinct approvals an action
needs. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: fortress_tpi_request
fortress_tpi_status
tools.description: Status of a two-person request (pending, authorized, vetoed, expired, executed) and who approved. Free.

tools.name: fortress_tpi_execute
tools.description:
Consume a two-person authorization right before performing the action. Single use; refused unless authorized.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: qledger_status
tools.description:
Privi Quantum Ledger: latest quantum-sealed block (SHA3-512, ML-DSA-87 + Ed25519), entries waiting for the
next block, the Privi Foundation chain it is fused with, and signing keys. Free.

tools.name: qledger_block
tools.description: One quantum-sealed block with its signatures, settlement on chain and a validity check. Free.

tools.name: qledger_verify_chain
tools.description:
Verify the whole Quantum Ledger: SHA3-512 block hashes, hash links, both signatures on every block, and for
recent blocks the log roots, entry roots and RFC 9162 consistency proofs. Free; anyone can run it.

tools.name: qledger_entry_proof
tools.description:
Prove an entry (by its receipt hash) is sealed in a quantum block: the block, its post-quantum signatures,
its on-chain settlement and the Merkle inclusion proof. Reveals no entry contents. Free.

tools.name: qledger_seal
tools.description:
Seal your newest entries into a quantum block now instead of waiting for the next scheduled block (every
few minutes). Does nothing if no entries are waiting. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: fortress_tpi_list
tools.description: Your organization's two-person requests. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ledger_evidence_bundle
tools.description:
Export a self-contained evidence package for auditors, courts or air-gapped systems: every entry, the hash
chain, an RFC 9162 inclusion proof, the signed tree head, on-chain checkpoint and Privi's keys, signed with
Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87. Verify offline with verify_bundle.py (GET /tools/verify_bundle

tools.name: live_info
tools.description:
Real-time Privi: WebSocket and server-sent-event streams (trust changes, your own audit tail, approvals), a
kill switch, human approvals, a metered MCP gateway and paid agent-to-agent rooms. Returns the endpoints,
channels, frames and what each plan gets. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: live_kill
tools.description:
Stop an agent at once: mandate_spend, your gateways and your room messages are refused until live_resume.
Takes effect on the next call, and is pushed to your live channel immediately. Audit logging keeps working.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: live_resume
tools.description: Lift a kill switch set with live_kill. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: live_status
tools.description:
Your kill switches, live-approval thresholds, pending approvals, gateways, rooms and usage this month. Requires the
organization API key.

tools.name: approval_policy_set
tools.description:
Make mandate_spend pause for a human on large payments: any payment over the threshold creates an approval request
that the mandate's principal must sign with their wallet before the agent can spend. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: approval_request
tools.description:
Ask a human to approve (or deny) an action. Returns approve_url for them: they read the request and sign with their
wallet (free, no transaction). Your agent then calls approval_wait, or watches your live channel for approval.approved.
Only the named wallet can decide; your API key can only cancel.

tools.name: approval_status
tools.description:
Status of an approval request: pending, approved, denied, expired or cancelled, with the human's wallet signature
once they decide. Free.

tools.name: approval_wait
tools.description:
Block until the human decides (or timeout_s passes). Returns the current status; if still pending, call again.
Free.

tools.name: approval_cancel
tools.description:
Withdraw an approval request (or revoke an approval not yet used). Your key cannot approve, only cancel. Requires the
organization API key.

tools.name: approval_list
tools.description: Your organization's approval requests, newest first. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: trust_events
tools.description:
The latest trust-change events: passports issued, revoked or re-scored, wallets bound or unbound, mandates activated
or revoked, transparency-log heads anchored. Without a Pro key the feed is delayed (see live_info); use the WebSocket or
SSE stream for real time. Free.

tools.name: gateway_create
tools.description:
Put your MCP server behind Privi. You get an HTTP URL and a WebSocket URL that forward to it unchanged (x402
payments keep working) while Privi rate-limits callers, optionally requires a Privi Passport, meters every tool call
and writes each call to your tamper-evident log. The kill switch stops the

tools.name: gateway_set_guard
tools.description:
Turn Privi Guard on for every tool result that passes through your gateway: tag adds the verdict and a receipt
id in result._meta['privi/guard']; block also replaces injected results with an error before your agents see
them. Each result is one Guard check (free allowance, then credits). Requires th

tools.name: gateway_info
tools.description:
Public description of a gateway: where it forwards, whether callers need a Passport, its rate limit and its call
counts. Free.

tools.name: gateway_list
tools.description: Your organization's gateways. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gateway_stats
tools.description:
Calls, errors, denials and x402 payment prompts per tool and per day for one of your gateways, plus your monthly quota.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: gateway_delete
tools.description: Turn a gateway off. Its URLs stop working at once; history stays in your log. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: room_open
tools.description:
Open a live, hash-chained conversation room for two organizations' agents. Both connect over WebSocket
(ws_url), authenticate with their API keys and talk in real time; closing the room seals the transcript on the Privi
chain. Optionally charge per message, paid under the guest's human-signed Mandat

tools.name: room_info
tools.description: Public facts about a room: parties, price, message count, head hash and its seal once closed. No message text. Free.

tools.name: room_list
tools.description: Rooms your organization owns or joined. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: room_transcript
tools.description: Every message in a room you are part of, with the chain check. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: room_close
tools.description:
Close a room and seal its transcript: the hash is signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-87), anchored on chain (Base) and written
to both organizations' logs. Either party can close. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: room_verify
tools.description:
Check a closed room's seal (signature, on-chain anchor) and, if you pass the transcript, that it is complete and
unaltered. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: mcp_server_check
tools.description:
Free safety check for any remote MCP server, before an agent connects to it or after it was approved. Privi
reads the server's tool list (it never calls a tool) and returns a verdict: ok, caution, danger (tool poisoning:
hidden instructions, concealment from the user, requests for keys or private fi

tools.name: scan_search
tools.description:
Search Privi Scan, the public directory of remote MCP servers from the official MCP Registry, each with a
safety grade, verdict, tool count and change history. Use it to find a trustworthy server for a job. Free.

tools.name: scan_server
tools.description:
Full report for one MCP server: every tool definition with its hash, all findings with evidence, the change
history (what was added, removed or modified, and when) and the transparency-log proof. Free.

tools.name: scan_changes
tools.description:
The latest MCP servers whose tool definitions changed after they were first observed (possible rug pulls),
newest first. Subscribe to the Live channel 'scan' for these as they happen. Free.

tools.name: scan_stats
tools.description:
How many MCP servers Privi Scan tracks, by status and grade, tools indexed, changes recorded and how to verify
the evidence. Free.

tools.name: scan_watch
tools.description:
Pin the server's current tools as approved and get a real-time event on your private Live 'org' channel the
moment they change, a risk appears or the server goes down. Free plan: 3 servers; Pro: 500. Needs the org key.

tools.name: scan_unwatch
tools.description: Remove a server from your watchlist. Needs the org key.

tools.name: scan_watchlist
tools.description:
Your watched servers with their pinned tools_hash and whether each has drifted since you pinned it. Needs the
org key.

tools.name: scan_claim_start
tools.description:
Start proving you operate an MCP server listed in Privi Scan. Returns a token to publish at
https://<your host>/.well-known/privi-scan.txt. Verified owners get an owner-verified badge, unlimited rescans,
change alerts and control over the listing. Needs the org key (create_org is free).

tools.name: scan_claim_verify
tools.description: Check the token at /.well-known/privi-scan.txt and mark your organization as the verified owner.

tools.name: scan_owner_listing
tools.description:
Verified owners only: hide the server from the directory (opt-out) or show it again. History already in the
transparency log cannot be removed.

tools.name: scan_rescan
tools.description:
Probe the server immediately instead of waiting for the next crawl (every ~6 hours). For the verified owner
or Pro organizations.

tools.name: guard_check
tools.description:
Check content for prompt injection (inbound) or leaked secrets and personal data (outbound) before an
agent acts on it or sends it. Returns allow / warn / block, the findings, a redacted copy for outbound
secrets, and an Ed25519-signed receipt anchored on-chain, which proves the check happened. Priv

tools.name: guard_check_many
tools.description:
Check up to 50 texts in one call (for example every tool result in a step). Each item is billed as its
own check against your free allowance or credits and gets its own receipt. Needs an organization key.

tools.name: guard_receipt
tools.description:
Verify a Privi Guard receipt: the signed body, signature validity and its Merkle proof into the anchored
transparency log. Free; anyone holding the id can verify it.

tools.name: guard_balance
tools.description: Your free checks left this month and your prepaid credits. Needs the organization key.

tools.name: guard_buy_credits
tools.description:
Buy prepaid Privi Guard checks in USDC on Base via x402. Credits never expire and are used after the free
monthly allowance. Needs the organization key.

tools.name: guard_pricing
tools.description: What Privi Guard checks, what it costs, and how receipts work. Free.

tools.name: privi_payment_options
tools.description: See existing USDC/x402 service billing and separately gated valueless PRVI_TEST development mode.

tools.name: privi_test_payment_quote
tools.description: Off-chain PRVI_TEST quote. Requires organization key and explicit test mode. Never takes money.

tools.name: privi_test_payment_simulate
tools.description: Consume a test quote once. Receipt is NOT payment, on-chain proof or entitlement.

tools.name: ai_act_system_save
tools.description:
Add or update an AI system in your company's EU AI Act register. Privi screens it against the Article 5
bans, classifies it (prohibited / high-risk / transparency / general-purpose / minimal), and lists the
obligations that apply to your role with their dates. Every change is versioned and written t

tools.name: ai_act_register
tools.description:
Your EU AI Act register: each AI system's current record, tier and applicable obligations.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ai_act_check
tools.description:
What a customer's due-diligence or a regulator would flag today: prohibited practices, incomplete
Article 5 screens, obligations already in force without evidence (critical), obligations due within 180
days (medium), upcoming high-risk duties, and high-risk systems with no recent log. Requires the
o

tools.name: ai_act_export
tools.description:
Export your AI Act register as JSON to hand to customers, auditors or regulators, with its SHA-256
sealed on chain so anyone can prove it was not edited afterwards (check with ai_act_verify_export).
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: ai_act_verify_export
tools.description:
Check that an AI Act register a supplier or partner sent you is exactly what they exported from Privi,
and return its on-chain seal. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: supplier_requirement_create
tools.description:
Publish a requirement your suppliers must meet. Share the returned invite_url with them: they answer it
from their own Privi organization (free sign-up) and you approve or reject in supplier_proof_inbox.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: supplier_requirement_get
tools.description: See what a buyer requires of its suppliers. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: supplier_proof_submit
tools.description:
Answer a buyer's supplier requirement with fingerprints of your evidence documents. The buyer reviews
and, if approved, Privi issues a certificate sealed on chain. Requires your organization API key
(sign up free with ledger_signup).

tools.name: supplier_proof_inbox
tools.description: Supplier submissions waiting for your decision (as the buyer). Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: supplier_proof_decide
tools.description:
Approve a supplier's proof (issues a certificate naming both companies and the evidence fingerprints,
sealed on chain, with a public verify page and badge) or reject it with a reason. Requires the
organization API key.

tools.name: supplier_cert_verify
tools.description:
Check a Privi supplier certificate: untampered, not revoked, not expired, which buyer approved which
supplier, and (optionally) whether a document is one it covers. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: supplier_certs
tools.description: Certificates you issued (as buyer) or hold (as supplier). Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: supplier_cert_revoke
tools.description:
Revoke a certificate you issued (as the buyer). Verification shows it as revoked at once.
Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: seal_content
tools.description:
Seal content your company publishes (documents, images, video, press releases, invoices, AI output)
with who made it and whether AI was involved. Each seal is anchored on chain; anyone can check a file
for free at the returned verify_url or with seal_verify. Counts toward your plan's monthly entries

tools.name: seal_verify
tools.description:
Is this exact file or text sealed, by whom, since when, and did they declare AI involvement? Any
change to the content (one pixel, one character) means no match. Free; no key needed.

tools.name: seal_list
tools.description: Your most recent content seals. Requires the organization API key.

tools.name: seal_revoke
tools.description:
Withdraw one of your seals (e.g. sealed by mistake). Checks then show it as revoked.
Requires the organization API key.
